entries.title: Proverbs 13:1
segments: Scorner; a child who is "wise in his own eyes," and therefore despises his father's admonitions and counsels.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:2
segments:
The fruit of his mouth; his wise words. 
 
  Eat violence; be violently destroyed.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:3
segments:
Openeth wide his lips; utters all his thoughts inconsiderately. 
 
Our comfort and prosperity in this world, and our eternal welfare after death, are greatly dependent upon the use we make of the gift of speech.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:4
segments: All riches, spiritual and temporal, are the price of industry: they who will not toil for them must remain poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:5
segments: False and deceitful men generally come to shame in the present life, and their reward hereafter must be "shame and everlasting contempt."

entries.title: Proverbs 13:6
segments:
Keepeth him that is upright; is his guardian and guide. 
 
Righteousness is a sure guide.  She leads the soul to God and blessedness.  But sin flatters men only to reward them with disappointment and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:7
segments: Maketh himself rich--maketh himself poor; some understand these words of the affectation of wealth, or poverty; but they rather contrast with the vain show of wealth its opposite virtue, an humble and unostentatious spirit.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:8
segments:
Are his riches; he is often compelled to buy his life by giving up his riches to his oppressors. 
 
  Heareth not rebuke; his poverty exempts him from the threats and spoilations to which the rich are subjected.  This proverb is peculiarly applicable to the despotic governments of the East.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:10
segments:
Wisdom; to avoid contention. 
 
Pride is the root of all contentions.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:11
segments:
Vanity; dishonest practices of every kind. 
 
  Labor; honest industry. 
 
Valuable possessions are gained by labor.  They who seek wealth, place, or influence by cunning and dishonesty, will in the end be disappointed.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:12
segments: It is good to set our hearts on God's promises, and not on this world; for he will fulfil the highest desires of those who put their trust in him.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:13
segments: The word; of divine admonition.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:14
segments:
Law; instructions and counsels. 
 
  To depart; teaching men to depart.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:15
segments: Hard; bringing upon them misery and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:17
segments:
A wicked messenger; one unfaithful to him who sends him. 
 
  Health; gives prosperity and joy. 
 
He who has proved himself worthy of being trusted will be trusted again, and thus he will rise to honor and influence; but they who betray the confidence reposed in them must come to speedy ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:18
segments: When we see an ignorant, self-conceited youth making light of God's words, and the counsels of his parents, we may know that he is on the road to a miserable and ignominious end.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:19
segments:
Desire; the holy desire of the good. 
 
  It is abomination to fools to depart from evil; evil is all their delight.  They have no holy desires whose accomplishment can make them blessed.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:20
segments: A great part of wisdom lies in the choice of our companions; for what they are, they will make us also.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:21
segments: Pursueth; as an avenger.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:22
segments:
To his children's children; which shall descend to them by God's blessing. 
 
  Is laid up for the just; God will take it from them and give it to the just. 
 
The best provision that a man can make for his family is to fear the Lord always, and to train them up in his fear.  An estate gotten by wickedness has the curse of God upon it, and cannot be expected to benefit those who inherit it.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:23
segments: Tillage of the poor--want of judgment; the poor man that tills the soil with patient industry shall have plenty of food; but he who despises honest labor, and seeks to live by unrighteous means, shall come to poverty and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 13:24
segments: Neglect of timely chastisement is cruelty to a child, for the want of early discipline ends in profligacy and misery.
